title: The founder of Hinge raised $18M to build a new AI dating service, Overtone
slides: Can AI fix what dating apps broke?
It analyzes voice, not just text.
You will know compatibility before meeting.
Try one voice call before matching again.
thread_text:
1. A voice before a match

Overtone just raised $18M to analyze how you sound, not just what you type. Your compatibility score arrives before the first date.

2. Why text fails

Written bios are curated. Your voice reveals hesitation, pace, and tone — data text can't capture.

3. The founder's bet

Overtone’s founder raised $18M on a single premise: voices predict chemistry better than profiles.

4. The system in action

One voice call. Then the algorithm tells you if you're compatible before you meet in person.

5. Try it this week

On your next dating app, request a voice call before swiping again. Would you trust that read?

instagram.caption:
Your next dating app match might be rejected by an algorithm before you even meet.  

Hinge's founder just raised $18M for Overtone, an AI that analyzes your voice—hesitation, tone, pace—not just your text bio. One call, then a compatibility score.  

For anyone creating a dating profile: how you *sound* now overrides the words you carefully choose.  

Would you let an algorithm judge your chemistry on a 3-minute voice call?
